# Adapt your Module 2 report

This file is the destination for the report you created in Module 2. Do not
write a second report from scratch. Instead:

1. Copy your Module 2 `.qmd` file over this file, keeping the name
   `4_report.qmd`.
2. Copy any local files it needs, such as `references.bib`, into this directory.
3. Keep the report structure and dynamic-reporting features you already wrote.
4. Adapt its code chunks to read and present the Snakemake workflow outputs.

The report is rendered from `demo/snakemake/`, so these paths are available:

| Path | Produced by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `work/1_names_clean.csv` | `1_clean.py` | Zurich names data with English column names |
| `work/2_yearly_winners.csv` | `2_summarize.R` | most common names by year and sex, including ties |
| `work/3_top_names.csv` | `3_prepare_plots.py` | top names by sex for 2021–2025, including cutoff ties |
| `work/3_selected_names.csv` | `3_prepare_plots.py` | yearly births for Peter and Daniel |

At minimum, adapt your report to:

- replace the Module 2 download and transformation code with reads of the
  workflow-generated CSV files;
- display `2_yearly_winners.csv` as the captioned table;
- recreate the top-names and names-over-time plots from the prepared inputs,
  retaining their figure labels and cross-references;
- include a value computed with inline code; and
- report the R or Python environment used to render it.

After each edit, run:

```bash
snakemake --cores 1
```

Then open `results/4_report.html`. When only this file changes, Snakemake
re-runs the report rule while leaving the upstream analysis outputs untouched.
